common_name: Large Holarctic Sap-Flux Fly (Large Blastoderm Embryo & 6-Chorion-Filament Egg)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila virilis (3.1 µm, detail scale)

paleobiology.age_note: All three chronospecies are Holocene (0 Ma). The step is a morphospace step at fixed age, not a stratigraphic transition.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: u_t = Du lap u + a - u + u^2 v; v_t = Dv lap v + b - u^2 v
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.turing_conditions: tr(J) < 0, det(J) > 0, Dv f_u + Du g_v > 0, (Dv f_u + Du g_v)^2 > 4 Du Dv det(J)

parameters.note: Du and Dv are shared by the three Holocene species. Only basal activator production a changes. Du is the unique positive diffusivity that places D. virilis (a = 0.10, Dv/Du = 10, b = 0.90) at lambda = 3.101 um. These are not the 136 um sibling power-law coefficients.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 dispersion relation and the critical-wavenumber selection law
Schnakenberg 1979 two-species kinetics and the homogeneous steady state u0 = a + b
Gompel et al. 2005: Drosophila abdominal pigment differences among species are cis-regulatory, including posterior bands in the melanogaster subgroup
Kondo and Miura 2010: reaction-diffusion as a framework, not a demonstration that D. virilis ocelli are Turing patterns
reconstructed_in_script: Shared Du, Dv with species-specific a so that D. virilis selects 3.101 um
Teissieri a = 0.058 (shorter selected wavelength, still unstable) and willistoni a = 0.360 (Turing boundary crossed)
Tergite mode counts from atlas adult lengths divided by seven
does_not_claim: That a published measurement fixes the D. virilis ocellus wavelength at 3.101 um
That the habitus photograph resolves 3.1 um pigment granules
That chorion-filament number is an input to this wavelength law
That willistoni lost a Turing pattern in the fossil record (all three species are extant at 0 Ma)
